model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, y-axis in percent) for six different methods: Base (black solid line with circle markers), FT (blue solid line with downward triangle markers), IKE (red solid line with upward triangle markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), a purple line with pentagon markers (labeled in legend but not named), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major gridlines and tick labels at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear, spanning from 35% to 65% with major ticks every 5%. As co-occurrence number increases, all methods generally show an upward trend in accuracy, though at different rates. ROME starts at ~51% at co-occurrence 1 and rises steadily to ~66% at 10⁴. MEND begins at ~44% and climbs to ~56%. The purple line starts near 44% and reaches ~55%. IKE starts at ~43% and increases to ~49%. FT begins at ~40% and rises to ~48%. Base starts at ~38% and plateaus around 44% after 10², showing the smallest improvement.
